text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert — streaming tail latency spike for /v1/stream (hosted). p95 up from 280ms to 1.8s, p99 up to ~6.2s. Auto-paging to on-call.
elena: saw the alert, looks like sudden increase in stalled chunks, clients reporting long idle windows. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.company/streams/rumble (graphs attached)
elena: reproducer: curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?prompt=hi\" — sometimes no chunks for ~4-6s, then big burst.
matt: I'm oncall, grabbing it. starting triage: which layer first? proxy or runtime?
jia: logs show repeated 504s and a lot of upstream write timeouts from the gateway (envoy) around the spike window. stack traces show kernel-level socket EPIPE occasionally.
sam: we also have increased connection counts to a handful of customers, one tenant has long-running chat sessions. could be client backpressure + proxy buffering.
elena: p95/p99 by region: us-west p99 7.1s, eu p99 4.8s, apac unaffected. traffic shift from us-west -> trying to correlate with deploys.
incident-bot: Recent deploys: eng-runtime @ 1778640000, eng-platform @ 1778639000. No rollback flagged.
matt: rolling deploys didn't overlap with spike window but worth checking runtime kernels for recent socket code. elena, can you tail the runtime logs for stalled chunk flushes?
elena: tailing /var/log/runtime/streaming.log — seeing repeated \"kv-cache-flush delayed by 3s\" and \"chunk-enqueue blocked\" messages. Pasting sample: ```[1778643205] WARN chunk-enqueue: blocked 312ms queue=128
[1778643206] WARN kv-cache-flush delayed 3012ms
[1778643207] ERROR writev: broken pipe\```
jia: envoy logs: ```upstream response body stream closed before end of stream, route: /v1/stream, downstream_remote_address: 10.34.0.21:43122``` looks like proxy closed connection before runtime finished sending.
sam: could be proxy_buffering enabled at the gateway causing backpressure when runtime stalls; if proxy buffers fill, it signals backpressure and runtime stalls.
matt: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable proxy buffering for streaming routes, 2) bump envoy proxy_read_timeout and idle_timeout, 3) enable fallback synchronous (polling) route for affected tenants. Which one is fastest?
elena: disabling proxy buffering is config change on gateway, low risk. I can patch and reload gateway config.
jia: bumping proxy timeouts needs infra approval but quick patch possible. fallback route needs code change and rollout -> slower.
matt: do the quick config changes first. elena, apply proxy buffering off for /v1/stream and increase read_timeout to 120s. Post command you will run?
elena: running: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway-streaming-tweaks
data:
  envoy.yaml: |
    route_config:
      per_route_buffering: false
      proxy_read_timeout: 120s
EOF
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway -n prod```
elena: applied and restarted gateway, rolling pods. watching metrics...
incident-bot: Gateway rollout started by elena at 1778643340.
matt: watching p99, p95 in 1 minute windows. also alerting customers via support_agent.
support_agent: pinging affected customer accounts with heads up: some users may see longer stalls; we're on mitigation. slack thread with CS opened: #cs-streams-1778643210.
(2m later)
elena: seeing p99 drop from ~6s to ~1.6s, p95 back to ~320ms. chunk throughput smoothing out.
jia: envoy error rate dropped significantly. upstream write errors decreased. kernel EPIPE counts down.
sam: looks like proxy buffering was the amplifier. still seeing occasional 1-2s stalls for a small fraction of requests — could be runtime GC or batching.
matt: can we improve headroom by increasing streaming worker pool on runtime temporarily? what's the safe limit?
elena: we can bump worker_count from 16 -> 24 on dedicated pools (config flag). doing gradual scale-up on a couple of cells now. command: ```curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.example/api/pools/scale -d '{"pool":"streaming-main","workers":24}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'```
elena: scaled two cells, CPU increase is modest. metrics show queue depth drop.
jia: collect flamegraph for the 1% tail if it persists. schedule probe at 1778643600.
matt: customer impact assessment: estimated affected requests ~3.1% of streaming traffic between 1778643180–1778643360. No data corruption, few 504s (0.4%), most recovered after reconnect. CS escalated one paying customer, we offered token credit.
support_agent: customer confirmed transient stalled UX; accepts credit. logging the conversation to CRM.
matt: for post-incident: action items: 1) runbook add proxy buffering as a known amplifier 2) add alert for proxy_write_backpressure metric 3) investigate root cause for runtime chunk-enqueue stalls (likely batching/queue pressure) 4) perf test client backpressure scenarios. owners: elena (runtime), jia (infra/envoy), sam (platform).
elena: I'll open GH issues: runtime#452 (chunk enqueue investigation) and runtime#453 (worker autoscale).
jia: infra will add envoy config guardrails and a dashboard for proxy buffering.
matt: keeping the incident open for 30m to watch for regression. if stable, will mark resolved and create postmortem doc.
(30m later)
matt: p95/p99 stable and error rate normalized. closing incident in 10.
incident-bot: Incident resolved at 1778643810. Summary: proxy buffering disabled + increased proxy timeouts + scaled runtime workers. Partial customer impact (3.1% of streams), mitigation applied, owners assigned for postmortem.
elena: adding notes to postmortem draft and tagging owners.
sam: thumbs up. :thumbsup:
